studies.title: A Fisher-Geometric View of Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
studies.problem: Determine which specialist changes can be consolidated through parameter merging and which residual discrepancies require additional isolated distillation.
studies.teacher_student_access: The main suite uses homologous SmolLM3-3B specialists; a Qwen3-4B math/code suite is secondary. Both compatible weights and probability scoring are required. Specialist-generated calibration completions precede branch-local student rollouts.
studies.method_details: Phase 1 solves a minimax subspace merge using unnormalized reward-second-moment residuals. Normalized residuals subsequently gate isolated per-domain OPD branches; selected updates are shrunk and remerged. The consolidated model receives no joint multi-teacher gradient.
studies.experiment_setup: Open-MOPD evaluates three domain means; G-OPD evaluates seven math/code tasks. Phase 2 alternatives start from the same Phase 1 merge and reuse branch updates when comparing write-back rules.
studies.reported_findings: Open-MOPD Table 1: Phase 1 macro is 32.52 versus 30.93 for the released 600-step OPD student; gated Phase 2 reaches 33.03. G-OPD Table 3: Phase 1/2 averages are 53.34/54.14 versus 53.79 for ExOPD. Section 4.1 reports less than two GPU-hours for unlabeled Phase 1 scoring; that is not the entire pipeline's cost.
studies.evidence_limits: The Fisher relation is local and second-order, not global equivalence between arbitrary merging and distillation. The practical minimax residual solution differs from a weighted Fisher stationary point. Only Phase 1 avoids gradient training; Phase 2 trains branches. Low residual is a coupled write-back diagnostic, not proof that a domain cannot improve by itself.
studies.survey_connection: A useful boundary case for the integration-position axis: merge, train branches, then remerge. Contrast with FuseChat's distill-then-merge ordering and shared-student MOPD; preserve parameter compatibility and two-stage cost accounting.

studies.reported_findings: For Qwen3-8B, MT-SDPO improves Macro by 4.64 and Worst by 14.79 points over the shared initialization, reducing Gap from 20.96 to 5.30. studies.experiment_setup: CodeContests and Polaris-53K training; three code and three math evaluations. studies.reported_findings: The full system has the highest reported means across the six tested benchmarks at both student scales; the 4B multi-agent system exceeds the single-agent 14B reference, with inference topology differing. Independent role policies are students, while contrasted teacher contexts share one set of frozen teacher weights; teacher count must follow learned components, not the number of scoring passes.

studies.integration_point: Offline example/token selection followed by supervised replay into one student, initialized from the final upstream checkpoint.
studies.caveat: Following MOPD does not make ROSS on-policy or multi-teacher. No new rollouts does not mean no extra model calls: reviewing, auditing and SFT cost remain. The annotation reviewer is not an independent human adjudication panel.
studies.problem: Verifier-positive trajectories can still contain locally incorrect, redundant or brittle tokens; imitating them all may undo upstream gains. Retained as the state-refresh boundary and as a contrast to selective online supervision.
studies.experiment_setup: Main model Qwen3.6-35B-A3B; saved Math-RL, Code-RL and three-domain MOPD histories. studies.reported_findings: On the six-benchmark MOPD panel, mean score is 58.40 upstream, 59.16 after continued MOPD, 57.70 after positive-rollout SFT and 62.20 after ROSS. These are author-reported results for that history and recipe. (Table 1). Holding retained examples and full context fixed, ROSS without the selective loss mask scores 58.49 versus 62.20 with it, isolating a mask contrast more cleanly than comparing differently filtered datasets. This uses a different generation/context protocol from single-turn experiments. (Table 2; Appendix C.4).
studies.evidence_limits: The main evidence is one MoE lineage with an additional 4B case; replay quality depends on available upstream histories and the strong annotation reviewer. Filtering comparisons alter dataset composition/size and supervised-token count; matched examples isolate masking but do not make every other baseline compute identical. Semantic categories assigned to 1185 sampled trajectories are model annotations, not verified universal error frequencies. Historical successes may be informative without proving generalization beyond the inspected evaluation sets.
